title: BCD to 7-Segment: Four Bits, Seven Lamps
topic: BCD-to-seven-segment decoder — a 4-bit binary-coded-decimal input (0000 through 1001) drives seven independent Boolean outputs, one per segment of a digit display. Each segment lights up for the set of digits where it should be on. Cycling through 0–9 makes the segment activation pattern visible.

beats.narration: How do four bits drive a seven-segment display? Each of the seven segments has its own logic equation.

elements.content: Four bits in — seven segments out.

beats.narration: Here's the seven-segment display, with segments labelled a through g. The four BCD inputs D three through D zero give us sixteen possible values, of which we use ten — zero through nine.

elements.content: Seven-segment digit on the right with segments labelled a–g
BCD input panel on the left — D3 D2 D1 D0
ten valid codes — zero through nine

beats.narration: Each segment is its own Boolean function of D three through D zero. For instance, segment a is on for every digit except 1 and 4. Karnaugh maps simplify each of the seven equations.

elements.content: seven Boolean functions, simplified by K-maps

beats.narration: Cycle the input from zero up to nine. Each new BCD code lights the segments that draw that digit — and the display reads the value.

elements.content: Seven-segment display redraws each digit in sync
one digit per second — segments follow

beats.narration: Seven small logic networks plus four input bits give you any decimal digit on a numeric display — the building block behind every clock, calculator and meter readout.

elements.content: Seven Boolean functions = one digit display.
every calculator, every clock, every digital meter
